resources.string: Tell me what you need. I\'ll do it on your phone.
Free compute comes from community members. They can see your task and screen.

Community miners or providers run your tasks with their own models.

Content is encrypted and relayed by the Tadolio platform. You still have to trust the platform. In theory it could swap the keys and read it.

Some miners use metered cloud APIs, so content passes through the company named.

They can see your task and screen, including chat, banking and other apps you ask it to open. If you prefer, use your own model.

Free use earns no coins.
Signing in is easiest. No key needed.
Turn on Accessibility so I can see and tap the screen for you.
I only do what you ask, and I always check with you before payments or messages.
① Downloaded apps → ② Tadolio → ③ Switch on
Just watch. I\'ll hand over when a screen-lock password or an “Allow” is needed.
It doesn\'t need internet, just a connection.
I\'ll notify you whenever I need your decision.
The code goes into a notification. Allow notifications first.
For payments, messages and deletions, I stop and ask first. If you\'re not in Tadolio, a notification is the only way to reach you. I also use it to tell you a task is done.
Newly installed apps must be unblocked first. Just once.
① ⋮ top right → ② Allow restricted settings → ③ Screen-lock password
Tap ⋮ top right → Allow restricted settings
Don\'t see it? Try another way
Android blocks Accessibility for apps installed from a browser, as a guard against unknown apps. You installed this one yourself, so unblocking it once is enough.
Another way: enter a 6-digit code once
Android will show 6 digits. Remember them, swipe down, and type them into Tadolio\'s notification.
① Remember the 6 digits → ② Swipe down → ③ Tap “Enter code”
Swipe down now to see it. It\'s already there.

The 6 digits are Android\'s Wireless debugging pairing code. They authorize Tadolio to start its built-in helper on this phone. They stay on the device, are never sent online, and are needed only once. After pairing I turn on Accessibility myself.
In About phone, find Build number and tap it 7 times.
① About phone → ② Build number ×7
① About device → ② Version → ③ Build number ×7
① About phone → ② Software information → ③ Build number ×7
Scroll down to Wireless debugging, turn it on, and tap Allow.
Turn on Wireless debugging, tap Allow
When the 6 digits appear, swipe down and type them into Tadolio\'s notification.
Tap Pair with code, remember the digits, then swipe down
Wrong or expired code. Tap it again for a new one.
The pairing window closed. Tap it again and re-enter.
Only do the step shown. Passwords, Accessibility switches and Allow prompts need your own tap.
Leaving the pairing window closes it. You can use split screen to see it while typing.
Keep Tadolio running in the background
You allow this in Android settings
Android asks you before allowing Tadolio to keep running in the background.
Choosing a provider means you agree to their service.
